chapter.hatman.2.sub: Every order is written down. Every debt.
chapter.hatman.3.sub: The party never ended. Nobody was allowed to leave.
chapter.hatman.4.sub: He has been taking your measurements all night.
chapter.hatman.5.sub: The table is set. One chair is empty.
obj.hatman.camp: Find Ruth's base camp. She said: the study, ground floor.
obj.hatman.camcorder: Take Ruth's camcorder from the desk
obj.hatman.casefile: Read Ruth's case file on the desk
obj.hatman.cellar_key: Find the cellar key. Ruth's file says: the hall table.
obj.hatman.cellar: Go down to the cellar. The door is in the stair hall.
obj.hatman.fuel: The generator is dry. Find fuel in the cellar.
obj.hatman.phone: The telephone in the entrance hall is ringing. The line was cut in 1962.
obj.hatman.evidence: Investigate the ground floor: the dining room, the living room, the kitchen (%s/3)
obj.hatman.clock: The maid's note: the workshop key is inside the grandfather clock
obj.hatman.workshop: Open the hatter's workshop in the cellar
obj.hatman.ledger: Search the workshop. There is a ledger on the desk.
obj.hatman.run_study: RUN. Get to Ruth's room and bar the door!
obj.hatman.upstairs: Unlock the gate on the stairs and go up
obj.hatman.masks: Look at the masks on the wall
obj.hatman.trail: Follow Ruth's trail upstairs: the child's room, the guest room, the bathroom (%s/3)
obj.hatman.recorder: Ruth hid her recorder in the master bedroom
obj.hatman.hide: HIDE. In the wardrobe. Camera OFF.
obj.hatman.run_hide: He saw you. Break his line of sight and hide!
obj.hatman.dressing: He is waiting outside the door. Leave through the dressing room.
obj.hatman.run_library: RUN. The library, end of the hall!
obj.hatman.hide_child: Locked! The child's room. Hide in the wardrobe!
obj.hatman.library: The library door has opened by itself
obj.hatman.attic: Climb to the attic. The ladder is in the upper stair hall.
obj.hatman.badge: Search the attic. There is something of Ruth's on the desk.
obj.hatman.run_cellar: RUN. All the way down. The workshop!
obj.hatman.servant: He is on the main stairs. The servants' stairs: through the library!
obj.hatman.hatblock: The hat block on the workshop counter. Pull it!
obj.hatman.ruth: Someone is sitting in the cold room
obj.hatman.dining: He is waiting in the dining room. You have his face.
obj.hatman.dining_safe: He is waiting in the dining room. (Marlowe's safe is in the master bedroom. The code is an invoice number.)
obj.hatman.tunnel: RUN. The front door is sealed. The cellar tunnel!
line.c1_dark: (No power. No light. Ruth's notes said she set up in the study.)
line.c1_camp: (Her bedroll. Her lantern, still burning. She left in a hurry... or she didn't leave.)
line.c1_file: ("Do not lie to him." Ruth doesn't write things twice unless she's scared.)
line.c1_glitch: (The camera just... caught something. Down the hall.)
line.c1_cellar: (Footsteps. Above me. Nobody else is supposed to be in this house.)
line.c1_gen_empty: (Generator. Tank's bone dry. There has to be fuel somewhere down here.)
line.c1_end: (He hung up. ...Something is walking down the stairs.)
line.c2_tv: (He was standing right behind the chairs. He was watching the film with me.)
line.c2_clock: (Thirty guests. No hosts. And the maid knew where the workshop key was.)
line.c2_shop: (Hat blocks. Felt. Mercury. And a ledger, open on the desk like someone was just reading it.)
line.c2_ahead: (He's in FRONT of me. How is he in front of me?!)
line.c2_window: (That was the window. We're on the ground floor. He's tall enough to knock on the top pane.)
line.c2_key: (Something slid out of the ledger's spine. A small brass key. For the gate on the stairs.)
line.c3_plates: (Thirty masks. Thirty brass plates. The newest one says CALLOWAY. And there is an empty hook.)
line.c3_bath: (Written in the dust on the mirror. Ruth's handwriting: DON'T LIE TO HIM.)
line.c3_recorder: (Ruth's bag. Her log says she hid the recorder in the master bedroom. The lock just clicked.)
line.c3_knock: (Three knocks. He's at the door. HIDE.)
line.c3_outside: (He closed the door behind him. Politely. ...He's still standing on the other side.)
line.c3_piano: (The piano. One note. He knows which door I used.)
line.c3_locked: (LOCKED. The boy's room, across the hall!)
line.c3_door_open: (The library door. He unlocked it. That's an invitation.)
line.c3_hatch: (Wood splintering above me. He tore the attic hatch open. He WANTS me up there.)
line.c3_key: (He put a key on the armrest before he left. The attic.)
line.c4_mirrors: (The mirrors. He is in every one of them. ...He is not behind me in any of them.)
line.c4_stairs: (He's coming UP the stairs. Other way. Library. Servants' stairs!)
line.c4_guests: (The guests. They're standing in the hall. They're all looking at me.)
line.c4_block: (Third hat block on the counter. Ruth's note. PULL IT!)
line.c4_safe: (He's stopped. He won't come in here. ...Why won't he come in here?)
line.c4_go: (The shelf is open. The whole house is quiet. He's letting me walk.)
line.c5_quiet: (Every lamp is lit. Every door is open. He has tidied up for company.)
line.c5_front: (Front door won't move. The tunnel in the wine cellar. GO!)
line.code: (Invoice No. 0731. Eleanor's letter said the safe opens with the order number.)
line.oil_and_fire: (Lamp oil and a lighter. This house is a hundred years of dry wood.)
line.caught0: (...I'm in the hall. I'm breathing. He put me back. Why did he put me back?)
line.caught2: (My face hurts. Like someone tried it on.)
line.caught3: (He is not trying to kill me. He is practising.)
line.hunt0: (The floor— he's coming up through the FLOOR!)
line.hunt2: (Don't run in a straight line. Doors. Put doors between us.)
line.tape0: Day six. I've stopped pretending this is a missing persons case.
line.tape1: He talks to me through doors. He asks permission. If I say no politely, he goes away. If I lie, the lights go out.
line.tape2: He can't see into a closed wardrobe. But the camera's little red lamp shines through the slats. I learned that the hard way.
line.tape3: He isn't hunting. He's shopping. He's trying us on. Thirty guests in 1962, and none of them fit.
line.tape4: If you're hearing this, %s— I told you not to come. ...He's knocking. Someone's knocking. Is that on the tape, or—
cut.intro.0: This is Detective Ruth Calloway. If you're hearing this, I've been inside Marlowe House longer than I planned.
cut.intro.1: Six trespassers missing in two years. I thought: squatters, a sinkhole, a bad floor. It isn't a bad floor.
cut.intro.2: There is someone in this house. He is very tall. He wears a hat. He knocks before he comes in.
cut.intro.3: My camera can see him when my eyes can't. I'm leaving it on the desk in the study, in case I... in case.
cut.intro.4: Don't come looking for me. I mean it. But if you do, because you never listen—
cut.intro.5: —whatever he asks you, do not lie to him.
cut.intro.6: (That message is nineteen days old. The front door is standing open.)
cut.power.1: (Light. The whole house is waking up.)
cut.power.2: (The dining room. There are... people. Sitting at the table. They've been sitting in the dark this whole time.)
cut.power.3: (...That telephone is not plugged into anything.)
cut.tv.0: ...on the first of November, nineteen sixty-two, police entered the Marlowe residence on Hollow Lane.
cut.tv.1: Thirty guests of a masquerade ball were found seated at the dinner table. None could say how long they had been there.
cut.tv.2: Of the hosts, hat-maker Edmund Marlowe, his wife Eleanor and their son Thomas, there was no trace.
cut.tv.3: One guest repeated a single phrase: "He asked so nicely."
cut.tv.4: (...That isn't the broadcast any more. That's this room.)
cut.masquerade.0: (Streamers. Paper hats. A birthday... and a ball. Sixty years of dust on a party.)
cut.masquerade.1: (Masks on the walls. Dozens. Each one with a little brass name plate.)
cut.masquerade.2: (That one is new. The plate isn't even tarnished. R. CALLOWAY.)
cut.masquerade.3: (And an empty hook. The plate is already engraved. It says %s.)
cut.fitting.0: (The attic. Mirrors. Hat stands. A tailor's fitting room... for hats.)
cut.fitting.1: (A row of hooks. A name under every one. Every person who ever went missing here.)
cut.fitting.2: (A hat box. New ribbon. The card says: FOR %s. He has been making it all night.)
cut.supper.0: (Thirty masks turn to look at the door. Nobody is breathing. I don't think they need to.)
cut.supper.1: (One chair is empty. There's a place card. I don't have to read it.)
cut.supper.2: Detective. You knocked this time. Do sit down.
cut.end_closed.0: ...Sixty-four years. I had forgotten the shape of it. Thank you. The account is closed.
cut.end_closed.1: I have no further business with this house. Or with the people in it. Good night, Detective.
cut.end_closed.2: At 6:02 AM the front door of Marlowe House opened by itself. Thirty-one people walked out into the rain. They did not remember the party.
cut.end_closed.3: You still owe me twenty for the Delgado stakeout. ...Take me home, rookie.
cut.end_closed.4: Case 0731, Marlowe House. Status: CLOSED. Paid in full.
cut.end_newface.0: There. It fits. I knew it would. I measured you in every doorway.
cut.end_newface.1: By morning there was a new mask on the wall of the upper hall. The brass plate under it had been engraved for some time.
cut.end_newface.2: Three weeks later another detective parked at the gate of Marlowe House, listening to an old voicemail. It was your voice.
cut.end_worn.0: You put the face on. It was cold. It was the right size for nothing human. And suddenly you were very, very tall.
cut.end_worn.1: Ah. So that is how it is done. I had wondered for sixty-four years. Good evening... sir.
cut.end_worn.2: The chair at the head of the table is never empty. Someone always knocks. Someone always asks so nicely.
cut.end_ashes.0: Marlowe House burned for nine hours. The fire brigade could not get the front gate open until it was over.
cut.end_ashes.1: They found no bodies. They found thirty-one masks in the ashes, unburnt. They found no trace of Detective Ruth Calloway.
cut.end_ashes.2: You drove until dawn. When you stopped, there was a hat on the passenger seat. It was still warm.
cut.end_cold.0: You came up out of the well with dirt under your nails and ran until the house was gone behind the trees.
cut.end_cold.1: He stood at the gate and did not follow. He tipped his hat. A guest who leaves may always come back.
cut.end_cold.2: Case 0731, Marlowe House. Status: OPEN. Detective Ruth Calloway: missing. Some nights, at home, something knocks. Three times. Politely.
dlg.p1: Good evening. You are standing in my hall.
dlg.p2: You came in without knocking. That is not how one visits.
dlg.p2.0: I'm sorry. The door was open.
dlg.p2.1: Who is this? Where is Ruth Calloway?
dlg.p3a: An apology. How rare. The last one did not apologise for nine days.
dlg.p3b: A question for a question. That is fair. She is being fitted.
dlg.p3c: I have no self to identify, Detective. That is rather the whole difficulty.
dlg.p4: I shall ask you things tonight. Answer truthfully and we will get along. Did you come here alone?
dlg.p4.1: My team is right outside the gate.
dlg.p5a: Honest. And alone. Good. I prefer my guests one at a time.
dlg.p5b: ...No. They are not. Do not lie to me in my own house.
dlg.p5c: Silence is also an answer. A rude one.
dlg.p6: I am coming downstairs now. I will knock. I always knock.
dlg.k1: Detective. You ran. Guests do not run.
dlg.k3a: ...No. Very well. A closed door is a closed door. You have better manners than you know.
dlg.k3b: I have BEEN. It was dull. There was no one to talk to.
dlg.k3s: You do not answer. I will take that as a no. For tonight.
dlg.k4: You took my ledger from the workshop. Did you read it?
dlg.k4.0: Yes. Order 0731. A hat for a gentleman without a face.
dlg.k4.2: What did Marlowe take from you?
dlg.k5a: Then you know what I am owed.
dlg.k5b: Your thumb is on the page, Detective. I can hear paper.
dlg.k5c: Something I had only one of.
dlg.k5s: Quiet again. You will learn to answer me.
dlg.k6: Keep the book. Read it again. I shall be upstairs. They are having a party. They have been having it for a very long time.
dlg.l1: Sit, if you like. No? Stand, then. Ruth stood too. For the first three days.
dlg.l2: You have been through my rooms. Tell me, Detective: what do you think I am?
dlg.l2.1: A hallucination. Mercury fumes from the workshop.
dlg.l3a: ...Yes. Sixty-four years, and you are the first to say customer.
dlg.l3b: Then breathe deeper. See if I thin out.
dlg.l3c: I knocked. I waited. I asked. Which of us broke into whose house?
dlg.l4: Now a question that matters. The woman. Did she send for you, or did you come on your own?
dlg.l4.0: She told me not to come. I came anyway.
dlg.l5a: Disobedient. Loyal. She said you would be. She has been honest with me for some time now.
dlg.l5b: No. I have her voice, Detective. I have listened to all of it. She begged you to stay away.
dlg.l5s: You hold your tongue. She did that too, at first.
dlg.l6: One more. If I gave you a hat tonight, a good one, made to measure, would you wear it?
dlg.l6.1: If it means Ruth walks out of here.
dlg.l7a: Hm. We shall ask again when you have seen the fitting room.
dlg.l7b: A trade. I like trades. I have not had good luck with them.
dlg.l7c: ...Do not say that lightly in this house.
dlg.l7s: Then I will decide for you.
dlg.l8: The attic is open to you. Go up. See what I have made.
dlg.r1: ...Is that you? Don't come closer. Don't look at my face. There isn't one.
dlg.r2: Listen. I don't have long before he's back in my mouth. He isn't cruel. He's OWED. Marlowe took his face as a deposit and gave him a hat that didn't fit.
dlg.r2.0: I'm getting you out of here.
dlg.r2.2: How do I know you're really Ruth?
dlg.r3a: Not through that door you're not. Not while he holds the account.
dlg.r3b: You don't stop him. You pay him.
dlg.r3c: You don't. ...You still owe me twenty for the Delgado stakeout. He wouldn't know that. He never asks about money.
dlg.r4: There's a safe in the master bedroom. The invoice number opens it. His face is inside. Give it BACK. Don't lie to him, don't take the hat, and whatever you do, do not put the face on.
dlg.r5: He's set the table. He wants you in the dining room. ...Go. And hey. Thanks for not listening to me.
dlg.f1: Sit. No one has sat in that chair since nineteen sixty-two. I had it dusted.
dlg.f2a: You have been rude in every room of my house. You have lied to me, or cursed me, or both. I am out of patience, and I had a great deal.
dlg.f2b: You have been so very agreeable. Yes to this, yes to that. Do you know what a man who says yes to everything is, Detective? Mine.
dlg.f2c: You have been honest with me. More or less. That is more than Marlowe managed.
dlg.f3: Here is my last question. I ask it of everyone. Will you wear it?
dlg.f3.0: I have something of yours. (Show him the face.)
dlg.f3.3: (You try to say no. Nothing comes out.)
dlg.f3.4: I'll burn this house down first. (Tip the lamp oil over the table.)
dlg.f_silence: No answer. At my table. ...I will count to three.
dlg.f_face.0: In Marlowe's safe. He never meant to give it back. I do.
dlg.f_face2: ...Paid. In full. By a stranger. I have no words for this, and I have had so many.
dlg.f_wear: It is cold. It fits nothing human. Around the table, thirty masks bow their heads.
dlg.f_yes: Then hold still. This will not hurt. That is what they tell me, afterwards.
dlg.f_no: No. ...Then you are a guest who is leaving. I will count to three. I am not good at counting.
ending.hatman.closed.0: You gave back what was taken. He kept his word. He always keeps his word.
ending.hatman.closed.1: Thirty guests and one detective walked out of Marlowe House at dawn.
ending.hatman.closed.2: The house was demolished the following spring. Nothing was found in the walls.
ending.hatman.closed.3: Somewhere, a tall gentleman is wearing his own face for the first time in sixty-four years.
ending.hatman.newface.1: There are thirty-two masks on the wall now.
ending.hatman.newface.2: He still does not have one of his own. But yours is a very good likeness.
ending.hatman.newface.3: Someone will come looking for you, %s. They always do.
ending.hatman.worn.0: Ruth told you not to put it on.
ending.hatman.worn.1: The account did not close. It changed hands.
ending.hatman.worn.2: You are very tall now. You are very patient. You always knock.
ending.hatman.worn.3: You are owed nothing. But you have so many questions to ask.
ending.hatman.ashes.0: You burned the house, the workshop, the ledger, and the debt.
ending.hatman.ashes.2: Ruth Calloway was never found. Neither were the guests.
ending.hatman.ashes.3: The hat on your passenger seat is your size.
ending.hatman.cold.0: You got out. That is more than most.
ending.hatman.cold.1: You left Ruth in the cold room. You left his face in the safe.
ending.hatman.cold.2: The file stays open on your desk. So does the door, some nights.
ending.hatman.cold.3: He knocks. He is still asking, very nicely.

note.hatman.case_file.title: Case File 0731 — R. Calloway
note.hatman.case_file.body:
MARLOWE HOUSE, 9 Hollow Lane.
Six missing persons in two years. All trespassers. No bodies.

Before that: 1 Nov 1962. Thirty masquerade guests found seated at dinner, unharmed, no memory. The hosts, the Marlowe family (hatters), never found.

WHAT I KNOW AFTER FIVE NIGHTS:
- Power: generator in the cellar. Cellar key is in the hall table by the telephone.
- There is a man in this house. Very tall. A hat. I cannot always see him. The camcorder ALWAYS can.
- He knocks. He asks. He waits for an answer.
- DO NOT LIE TO HIM.
- Do not lie to him.

If I am not at this desk, take the camera. Take the batteries. Read everything. He likes it when people read.
note.hatman.ruth_rules.title: Ruth's Rules (taped inside the drawer)
note.hatman.ruth_rules.body:
1. He does not move while you are looking at him. In the dark, you are NOT looking at him. Use the camera.
2. The camera eats batteries. Do not leave it on.
3. Stare at him too long and he gets tired of the game. Look, back away, break the line. Do not hold the stare.
4. He cannot see into a closed wardrobe. Camera OFF inside. The little lamp shows through the slats.
5. If he saw you climb in, the wardrobe is a coffin. Hide BEFORE he comes round the corner.
6. A barred door is a closed door. He respects a closed door. Mostly.
7. When he asks you something: answer. Politely. Truthfully. "No" is allowed. Lies are not. Silence is worse than you think.
8. He is not angry. He gets angry. Those are different things. Keep them different.
note.hatman.photo.title: Photograph, 1962
note.hatman.photo.body:
(A family portrait on the front steps of the house. EDMUND MARLOWE in a bowler, ELEANOR beside him, and a boy of about eight, THOMAS, in a paper party hat.)

(Behind them, in the open doorway, there is a fourth figure. It is much too tall for the door frame. Someone has scratched at the emulsion where its face should be, with a pin, until the paper tore.)

(On the back, in pencil:)
He was not there when we took it.
note.hatman.newspaper.title: The Hollow County Courier, 3 Nov 1962
note.hatman.newspaper.body:
THIRTY GUESTS, NO HOSTS
Mystery at the Marlowe Masquerade

Police called to 9 Hollow Lane on Thursday found thirty guests of a masquerade ball seated at the dining table in complete darkness. The meal before them was untouched and, by the surgeon's estimate, four days old.

None of the guests could account for the time. None could be persuaded to remove their masks without considerable distress.

Mr. Edmund Marlowe, the well-known hatter, his wife and their young son have not been seen. Mr. Marlowe's workshop was found locked from the outside.

Asked who had kept them at table, one lady answered only: "The gentleman. He asked so nicely."
note.hatman.guest_list.title: Guest List — Thomas's Birthday Masquerade
note.hatman.guest_list.body:
31 October 1962. Dinner at eight. Masks at nine.

(Thirty names in Eleanor's careful hand. Dr. and Mrs. Hale. The Pembertons. Miss Ada Crane. Mr. Lowell of the bank...)

(At the bottom, in a different hand. The ink is brown, not blue, and the letters are far too tall and far too narrow:)

+1. The gentleman of Order 0731.
He will collect in person.
Please set a place.
note.hatman.maid.title: Notice — Mrs. Brandt, Housekeeper
note.hatman.maid.body:
Mrs. Marlowe,

I give my notice as of tonight and I will not be staying for the party.

It is the knocking, ma'am. On the pantry door, from the inside, when I know the pantry is empty. Three knocks, and then a gentleman's voice asking if he may come through. I said "no, sir" as I was raised to, and he thanked me. He THANKED me.

Mr. Marlowe says it is the pipes. Then Mr. Marlowe may answer the pipes himself.

The workshop key is where he always hides it from you: inside the case of the long clock in the hall.

Never tell that voice to come in.
— G. Brandt
note.hatman.phone_pad.title: Telephone Message Pad
note.hatman.phone_pad.body:
WHILE YOU WERE OUT

12 Oct — A gentleman rang about his order. Would not leave a name.
14 Oct — The same gentleman. Says he will call again.
15 Oct — Again.
15 Oct — Again.
19 Oct — He asks if the hat is ready. He asks if Mr. Marlowe still has "the deposit".
26 Oct — He says he will come and collect.

(The last entry is dated nineteen days ago. It is in Ruth's handwriting.)

He rang for me. The line is dead and he rang for me. He knew my name.
note.hatman.doctor.title: Letter from Dr. Hale
note.hatman.doctor.body:
Edmund,

I will be plain. The tremor, the sleeplessness, the conviction that you are being watched from doorways: this is mercury. Every hatter in England gets it in the end. It is the nitrate in your felt.

There is no tall customer. There is no order "paid in advance". You have been breathing poison in an unventilated cellar for twenty years, and your mind is making company for itself.

Close the workshop. Take Eleanor and the boy to the coast.

I will see you at the masquerade, where I intend to prove to you that your gentleman does not exist.
— Hale

(Under the signature, pencilled much later, in a shaking hand:)
He sat next to me.
note.hatman.ledger.title: Marlowe & Son — Order Ledger
note.hatman.ledger.body:
(A thick ledger. Thousands of orders: toppers, bowlers, mourning veils. One page has been read so often the spine falls open to it.)

ORDER No. 0731 — 7 July 1962
Customer: declines to give a name.
Item: one hat. Gentleman's. "To be made to measure."
Measure: customer has no head upon which a measure may be taken.
Payment: IN ADVANCE.
Deposit received: one (1) face. His own. Taken off at the counter and laid down like a glove.
Terms: deposit returnable upon delivery of goods.

(In the margin, later:)
I should not have taken it.
I should not have LOCKED IT UP.

(Something small and hard is sewn into the spine.)
note.hatman.making_log.title: Workshop Log — E. Marlowe
note.hatman.making_log.body:
12 July. Began 0731. The felt will not take the dye. It comes out of the vat the colour of a bruise and then goes black by itself overnight.

30 July. I cannot block it. Every block I own is too small. I have carved a new one from the cellar beam. It is the height of a child.

19 Sept. It is finished. It is the best work I have ever done and I cannot look at it.

2 Oct. He tried it on. It does not fit. It cannot fit: he has nothing to put it ON. He was very polite about it. He asked for his deposit back. I told him I had mislaid it.

I lied to him. In my own shop. The lamps went out, all of them, and he stood in the dark and said: "I shall wait."

30 Oct. Eleanor wants the party. I have put the deposit in the bedroom safe and the code on the invoice. Let him wait.
note.hatman.gen_log.title: Generator Maintenance Tag
note.hatman.gen_log.body:
PETROL GENERATOR — HOLLOW ELECTRIC CO.
Last serviced: Sept 1962.
Do not run in a closed room.

(Below, in ballpoint. Ruth:)

Night 2: Fuel can is in the wine cellar, in the trunk by the back wall. Enough for a few nights.
Night 4: It cut out at 3 AM with a full tank. Nothing wrong with it.
Night 5: Worked it out. It dies when I lie to him. I told him I had back-up coming. Every lamp in the house went dark and I heard him breathe in.
He doesn't break the lights. The lights just don't want to be on in a room where someone's lied.
note.hatman.cellar_list.title: Cellar Inventory
note.hatman.cellar_list.body:
WINE — 240 bottles, laid down 1948–1961.
COAL — 2 tons.
PRESERVES — see pantry book.

COLD ROOM — SEALED by order of Mr. Marlowe, 31 Oct 1962. Entry through the workshop ONLY. The household is not to ask about the cold room.

TUNNEL — the old ice passage runs from the back of the wine cellar to the garden well. Gate to be kept locked. Mr. Marlowe has the only key.

(Scratched into the wood of the shelf beside it, with something sharp:)
THE GATE IS NOT LOCKED. IT IS POLITE.
note.hatman.plates.title: The Brass Plates
note.hatman.plates.body:
(Under every mask, a small engraved plate.)

DR. A. HALE — 1962
MRS. HALE — 1962
MISS ADA CRANE — 1962
MR. LOWELL — 1962
(...twenty-six more, all 1962...)

J. OKAFOR — two years ago
M. REYES — two years ago
T. & S. WHITLOCK — last year
D. ARCENEAUX — last spring
P. NOVAK — last autumn

R. CALLOWAY — nineteen days ago
(This mask is not dusty. It is not porcelain either. It is warm.)

(And one empty hook. The plate beneath it is already engraved. The brass is still bright where the tool went in:)
%s
note.hatman.diary.title: Thomas's Diary
note.hatman.diary.body:
28 October
There is a tall man in the wall of my room. He knocks on the INSIDE of the wardrobe. I said who is it and he said A CUSTOMER and I said the shop is downstairs and he laughed. It was a nice laugh.

29 October
He says Father has something of his and won't give it back. He says that is called STEALING. I said Father doesn't steal. He said then your father LIES and that is worse.

30 October
He says if Father will not pay then somebody in the house must. I said I have 2 shillings. He said it is not that kind of owing.

31 October
It is my birthday. He asked could he come to the party. He asked SO nicely. Mother says never be rude to a guest.

I said yes.
note.hatman.drawing.title: A Child's Drawing
note.hatman.drawing.body:
(Wax crayon on butcher paper. A house with too many windows. A table with a great many small round faces along both sides.)

(At the head of the table sits a figure drawn in black, pressed so hard the crayon has gone shiny. It is three times the height of the others. It has a hat. It has no face: just the brown of the paper, left empty.)

(An arrow points to it:)
MY FREND
HE IS BORROWING EVERYBODYS UNTIL HE GETS HIS OWN BACK

(An arrow points to a very small figure beside it, wearing a paper hat:)
ME. I AM NEXT TO HIM BECAUSE I SAID YES FIRST.
note.hatman.ruth_bag.title: Ruth's Log — Night Nine
note.hatman.ruth_bag.body:
Can't use the study any more. He stands outside it.

Things I'm sure of:
He isn't Marlowe. He's what Marlowe cheated.
The guests downstairs aren't dead. They're being WORN. One at a time. He puts them on, he looks in the attic mirrors, he takes them off again. None of them fit.
I think he's going to try me next.

The recorder is in the master bedroom, on the night table. Everything is on the tape.

If you find this, rookie: he does my voice now. He's good. But he calls everybody "Detective" and he never talks about money. Ask me what you owe me. If I don't know, RUN.

I have been honest with him for four days. It's the only thing keeping my face on.
note.hatman.mirror_note.title: Tucked Behind the Mirror
note.hatman.mirror_note.body:
(A page torn from a police notebook, folded small.)

Night eleven.
I asked him straight out what he wants.

He said: "What I am owed. I gave a deposit. I received nothing. I have been very patient, Detective. I have asked every person who came through that door whether they could settle the account, and every one of them has lied to me, or cursed me, or said yes without understanding the question."

I asked what the question was.

He said: "Will you wear it?"

I think the right answer isn't yes and it isn't no. I think the right answer is something you have to be HOLDING.

I wrote on the glass in case I forget how to write.
note.hatman.eleanor.title: Eleanor's Letter (never posted)
note.hatman.eleanor.body:
Dearest Margaret,

Edmund keeps a FACE in the bedroom safe.

I am not mad and I am not being fanciful. I saw it when he opened the door to put the invoice book away. It is not a mask. A mask does not have pores. It lay on the green baize and its eyelids were shut and I swear to you they MOVED, the way a sleeper's do.

He says it is "security against an order" and that the safe opens only to the number of that order, which he has written on the unpaid invoice and hidden among his books upstairs so that I shall not find it.

Margaret, there is someone in this house who wants that thing back. He knocks on the walls at night and asks me, very gently, whether my husband is an honest man.

I have stopped being able to answer him.
— E.
note.hatman.invoice.title: Invoice — UNPAID
note.hatman.invoice.body:
MARLOWE & SON, HATTERS
9 Hollow Lane

INVOICE No. 0731

To: the gentleman (no name given)
For: one hat, bespoke

Price ............ PAID IN ADVANCE
Deposit held ..... ONE FACE
Balance due ...... NIL

Goods delivered? ..... NOT TO SATISFACTION
Deposit returned? .... NO

(Stamped across it, crooked, in red:)
ACCOUNT OPEN

(And underneath, in the tall narrow brown handwriting, very neat:)
I shall keep asking.
note.hatman.folklore.title: "The Gentleman Caller" (a marked page)
note.hatman.folklore.body:
...known in the northern counties as the Caller, the Long Guest, or simply the Gentleman. Accounts agree on these points:

He cannot enter where he has not knocked.
He cannot stay where he has been courteously refused.
He keeps every bargain to the letter and expects the same.
He may not harm one who has dealt honestly with him.

It follows that he is dangerous only to three sorts of person: the one who invites him without thought, the one who insults him, and, worst of all, the one who lies to him. A liar has broken faith first; with a liar he may do as he pleases.

It is said he has no face of his own, having pledged it once in a bargain, and that he wears a hat so that no one may see what is not under it.

(In the margin, in Marlowe's hand:)
God forgive me. He was only ever a customer.
note.hatman.ruth_tape.title: Ruth's Tape (transcript)
note.hatman.ruth_tape.body:
Day six. I've stopped pretending this is a missing persons case.

He talks to me through doors. He asks permission. If I say no politely, he goes away. If I lie, the lights go out.

He can't see into a closed wardrobe. But the camera's little red lamp shines through the slats. I learned that the hard way.

He isn't hunting. He's shopping. He's trying us on. Thirty guests in 1962, and none of them fit.

If you're hearing this, %s— I told you not to come.

...He's knocking. Someone's knocking. Is that on the tape, or—

(The tape runs on for eleven minutes of silence. Near the end, very close to the microphone, a man's voice says, kindly: "You may stop recording now.")
note.hatman.badge_note.title: Ruth's Badge, and a Note
note.hatman.badge_note.body:
(Detective's shield, HOLLOW COUNTY, No. 2214. Wrapped around it, a page in handwriting that gets worse as it goes.)

He's finished with the fitting. I don't have long with my own mouth.

I'm in the COLD ROOM. Cellar. Behind the south wall of the workshop: the shelving is a door. Pull the third hat block on the counter beside it. He won't follow you in there. It's where Marlowe hid from him, at the end. It didn't help Marlowe.

Marlowe's confession is in this desk. READ IT. There's a way to close the account and it isn't a gun and it isn't running.

He made you a hat. It's in the box by the hooks. Don't open it.

Rookie. He's standing behind you while you read this.
Don't turn round.
Just go.
note.hatman.confession.title: The Confession of Edmund Marlowe
note.hatman.confession.body:
1 November 1962, before dawn.

I am a hatter and a liar, and of the two it is the lying that has ruined us.

A customer paid me in advance. He paid with his FACE, because it was all he had, and I took it, God help me, because I wanted to see whether I could make a hat for such a thing. I could not. And when he asked for his deposit I told him it was lost, because I had grown used to looking at it.

He came to the party tonight. Thomas invited him. He sat at the head of my table and asked each of my guests, one after another, whether they would settle my account. They laughed. They said yes, as a joke.

He is trying them on now, upstairs. Eleanor first.

The remedy is simple and I am too great a coward for it: GIVE IT BACK. The face is in the safe. The number is on his invoice. Put it in his hands and say it is returned. He is bound to close the account. He is the most honest creature I have ever met.

Do not WEAR it. Whatever wears that face is the customer.
note.hatman.hatbox_card.title: The Card on the Hat Box
note.hatman.hatbox_card.body:
(A hat box, striped, tied with a new black ribbon. A card is tucked under the bow. The handwriting is brown, very tall, very narrow, and extremely neat.)

FOR %s

Made to measure.
I took the measurements myself: in the hall, on the stairs, and while you were reading at the desk downstairs. You hold very still when you read.

I have never yet made one that fits.
I have high hopes for this one.

We will try it on at supper.

(The box is not empty. Something inside it shifts its weight when you step back.)
note.hatman.safe_note.title: Deposit Tag
note.hatman.safe_note.body:
(A luggage tag on a loop of string, tied to the thing in the safe.)

DEPOSIT AGAINST ORDER No. 0731
Property of the customer.
Returnable on demand.

DO NOT WEAR.
DO NOT WEAR.
DO NOT

(The face is the size of a serving dish. It is pale and smooth and it is not porcelain. It has no eyes, only the places for them, and a mouth that has been sewn shut with something finer than thread.)

(It is breathing. Very slowly. It has been waiting in the dark for sixty-four years to be handed back.)

msg.hatman.phone_dead: No dial tone. The cord has been cut for sixty years.

msg.hatman.hook_you: An empty hook. The plate reads: %s. The engraving is fresh.
msg.hatman.hooks: A hat on every hook. A name under every hat.
msg.hatman.hatblock_stuck: A wooden hat block. It is fixed to the counter. Odd.
msg.hatman.hatblock_hint: The hat block on the counter by the shelves. PULL IT!
msg.hatman.safe_empty: The safe is empty. The baize is still warm.
msg.hatman.litter: Old papers. Nothing you can read.
msg.hatman.mannequin: A dress form. It is facing a different way than it was.
msg.hatman.ruth_coat: Ruth's coat, on a dress form. It has been taken in at the shoulders. Fitted.
msg.hatman.mirror_attic: You are the only one in the mirror. You count twice.
msg.hatman.mirror_bath: Written in the dust: DON'T LIE TO HIM
msg.hatman.host_chair: The head of the table. The cushion is pressed down.
msg.hatman.his_chair: The leather is cold. Something very tall sits here.
msg.hatman.shelf: Shelving. Solid. There is a draught coming through it.
msg.hatman.tunnelgate: An iron gate. It is not locked. It simply will not open for you yet.
msg.hatman.ruth_chair: A chair in the middle of the ice.
